[PRNewswire] OceanBase Global Revenue Doubles, Launches AI Platform
sum: BEIJING Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- OceanBase today announced its 2026 business milestones at the AI Data Conference held in Beijing. The company sustained robust growth trajectory throughout the year, achieving a revenue compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of over 60% in the past five years, driven by the rapid expansion of its AI data platform business and international markets.
In 2026, OceanBase's international revenue grew by 100% year-over-year, and now accounts for over 15% of its total revenue, while its international customer base grew by 300%.

Currently, OceanBase's international business is anchored in Southeast Asia and is expanding into Japan, the Middle East, and North Africa. OceanBase has been named the top distributed transactional database vendor in Asia and Oceania with a 15.5% market share based on 2025 revenue, according to an Omdia report released in September. So far, OceanBase has served over 20 leading e-wallets, more than 50 payment institutions, and over 30 fintech enterprises. Beyond fintech, traditional banks, including HSBC, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), and Hang Seng Bank, have begun choosing OceanBase to modernize their core systems.

Overall, the financial sector remains OceanBase's strongest market. To date, OceanBase supports 70% of China's mega-banks with over RMB 1 trillion in total assets, as well as over 100 major mid-sized banks, supporting more than 200 core business systems and stably hosting over 1,500 critical business systems. In the non-bank financial sector, OceanBase serves 95% of leading insurance institutions, 90% of top securities brokers, and 65% of leading asset management companies. Its share in the financial industry's distributed database market approaches 30%, securing the No. 1 position in the sector's on-premises deployment market for three consecutive years.

Revenue from AI-related businesses exceeded RMB 100 million. Currently, OceanBase's AI data capabilities are now deployed across manufacturing, consumer goods, healthcare, and embodied intelligence scenarios.

sum: On November 20, a release published by Associated Press said Ping An Digital Bank had received an additional capital injection of HKD 500 million from Lufax Holding. The funding is intended to strengthen the digital bank's capital base and support continued business expansion in Hong Kong.

Ping An Digital Bank is a wholly owned subsidiary of Lufax and a member of Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China. The bank operates under a full banking licence and serves retail customers and businesses in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area.

For retail customers, the bank's mobile application combines deposits, foreign exchange, cross-border remittances, wealth services and insurance. Its business banking strategy targets trade-focused small and medium-sized enterprises as well as cross-border e-commerce companies. The bank is also using commercial data in account opening and credit assessment.

Chief Executive Ronald Iu said the bank had recorded continued growth in assets and deposits after launching insurance and wealth services earlier this year. He added that the recent expansion into high-end wealth management through private funds had increased fee and commission income. Chairman Dicky Peter Yip said the fresh funding reflected confidence in the management team and the bank's long-term strategy.

The announcement gives Ping An's Hong Kong financial-services platform additional capital for expansion, while the operating outcome will depend on whether new services generate durable customer activity and fee income. The initiative also broadens the group's integrated finance offering beyond its established insurance and banking activities.

items.t: Caught Out By ZhongAn’s Fall? Here’s What The Bears Saw
sum: If you had skimmed past ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance at the start of 2026, thinking it looked too complicated or too hard to value, the skipped pain turned out to be very real. Investors who held ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance from the start of the year are down 48.8%, including dividends. The share price result is clear. The harder question is which assumptions and warnings, already on record before January, might have prompted closer scrutiny.
The move put ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance in the middle of this trade. Scan 16 top copper producer stocks for other companies exposed to it.
The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance
The shares cost HK$16.09 at the start of the period, and ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance sat between two very different stories about where its digital insurance model could go next.

The bullish narrative saw a Fair Value of HK$21.83, a notional target based on assumptions such as revenue increasing 9.3% and profit margins holding around 2.7% over a 3 year stretch, supported by AI tools and new products.

The more cautious view put Fair Value at HK$13.21, reflecting concerns that tighter data privacy rules, aging demographics and high expense ratios could compress margins and maintain earnings pressure.

The clearest fresh fact was the AM Best upgrade of ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance to an A financial strength rating with a stable outlook, which supported parts of the bullish quality argument. At the same time, H1 2026 figures showed revenue rising to C¥18,310.609m, net income up to C¥1,549.964m, and net margin moving from 4.2% to 8.5%, so the evidence leaned toward the optimistic case.

Ping An stock gets Citi Buy rating as operating recovery takes shape
sum: On Sunday, November 15, 2026, Citi published a research note on Ping An after hosting the group at its China Investor Conference. The study, carried by ReportGem, assigns the stock a Buy rating and focuses on a possible recovery in operating profit.

Citi says management expects operating profit attributable to shareholders to expand steadily. The research points to a gradually recovering life-insurance contractual service margin balance, continued new-business-value development and improving operating variances.

Banking is another central part of the assessment. Ping An Bank is moving closer to the end of its balance-sheet de-risking cycle, while product positioning, customer management and risk controls are improving. Citi also sees lower impairment pressure and stronger fee-based earnings supporting the asset-management business.

The study says new bancassurance rules introduced in July disrupted short-term sales by reducing frontline incentives. Management expects the transition to take three to six months to normalize, while Citi says underlying demand remains robust. The report cites a guaranteed return of 1.75 percent and a potential total return of about 3 percent for participating products as factors supporting demand.

Citi also highlights Ping An Securities, which it says has delivered more than 30 percent annual profit growth for three consecutive years and serves about 26 million retail customers. The broader group has about 250 million financial customers, creating scope for additional cross-selling across insurance, banking and investment services.

Ping An stock traded at 5.95 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:27 CET on Monday, November 16, 2026. The latest analyst view gives investors a fresh framework for weighing resilient operating businesses against the effects of investment-market swings and the ongoing bancassurance transition.

sum: Ping An reported resilient underlying performance for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as operating profit advanced while the group expanded artificial intelligence across its financial and healthcare businesses. The company announced the results on October 28 in a Ping An results release.

Operating profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million in the first nine months. Equity attributable to shareholders of the parent company reached RMB1,044,366 million at September 30, up 4.4 percent from the end of 2025.

Life and health insurance operating profit rose 5.7 percent to RMB87,238 million. Ping An P&C increased premium income 3.5 percent to RMB265,215 million, while its combined ratio improved by 1.4 percentage points to 95.6 percent. The bank also contributed to the result: revenue rose 2.4 percent to RMB103,100 million and net profit increased 2.2 percent to RMB39,186 million.

Ping An said its Express Service enabled AI-supported inquiry, consultation and processing in 90 percent of the group's business scenarios by September 30. The service had handled more than 150 million user sessions and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI.

Average daily token consumption exceeded 330 billion in September, more than ten times the December 2025 level. Token output per compute unit increased 509 percent, while cost per token declined 81 percent. The company presented these changes as support for scalability and efficiency, rather than as a standalone explanation for earnings.

AI Doctor served users more than 62 million times in the first nine months, and AI service representatives handled about 1,484 million interactions, equal to 82 percent of total customer service volume. Smart fraud detection generated RMB10.04 billion in claims savings for Ping An P&C, 9.7 percent more than a year earlier.

For investors, the results underline the difference between recurring operating progress and the sensitivity of reported performance to investment markets. Ping An said its insurance funds investment portfolio grew 5.2 percent from the start of the year to RMB6.83 trillion at September 30.

sum: Ping An Bank released its third-quarter report on October 24, covering the nine months ended September 30, 2026. A WallStreetCN report published by Futu said operating income rose 2.4 percent year over year to RMB 103.1 billion, while net profit attributable to shareholders increased 2.2 percent to RMB 39.186 billion.

Net interest income reached RMB 66.755 billion, up 0.3 percent from the same period a year earlier. The report said the third-quarter net interest margin reached 1.80 percent, supported by lower funding costs and efforts to improve the corporate liability mix.

Corporate loan balances stood at RMB 1.709026 trillion at the end of September, while corporate deposits reached RMB 2.386713 trillion. The average interest rate on corporate deposits for the first nine months fell to 1.28 percent, indicating progress in funding-cost management even as loan growth remained moderate.

Retail customers totaled 130.2789 million at the end of September, and retail assets under management rose to RMB 4,392.327 billion. Personal loans were more uneven: mortgage balances increased, while credit-card receivables, consumer loans and business loans declined from year-end levels.

The report also highlighted new artificial-intelligence-enabled card products and expanded digital service tools. For investors, the development points to Ping An Bank's effort to deepen customer engagement beyond traditional lending and deposit products.

The non-performing loan ratio was 1.05 percent at the end of September, unchanged from year-end 2025, while the loan-loss reserve coverage ratio stood at 214.75 percent. The corporate-loan non-performing loan ratio was 0.89 percent, compared with 1.20 percent for personal loans.

items.t: Insurance Partnership Could Shape What Comes Next For WeRide Stock
sum: WeRide announced a global insurance partnership program with Allianz Insurance Singapore and Ping An Property & Casualty to support autonomous driving services across existing operations in China, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, as well as planned launches in Europe, with coverage spanning liability, product risks, privacy and cybersecurity.

The initiative targets full lifecycle insurance for WeRide’s roughly 3,600 autonomous vehicles, including more than 1,800 Robotaxis. It aims to streamline risk coverage across markets and support unit economics as deployments scale through platforms such as WeRide Go, Uber and TXAI.
We will examine how WeRide’s investment narrative is influenced by this global insurance partnership program that targets lifecycle coverage for L4 fleets.

To own WeRide, you need to believe large scale L4 fleets can move from heavy investment to more self funded growth. The global insurance partnership speaks directly to that thesis. It targets consistent coverage across roughly 3,600 autonomous vehicles, which could help shorten deployment lead times and support the push for higher vehicle utilization in more cities.

The immediate catalyst still sits with new fully driverless permits and proof that Abu Dhabi style economics travel into other high fare markets. The biggest near term risk remains cash burn from R&D and expansion if ride volumes, pricing or partner demand through platforms like Uber and TXAI do not line up with that larger fleet footprint.

The new global insurance program is tightly linked to those permitting and utilization catalysts. Allianz Insurance Singapore and Ping An bring local expertise in multiple jurisdictions, which may simplify how WeRide structures liability, product, privacy and cybersecurity coverage as it moves from pilot zones to broader city operations in China, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

Framing this against the rest of the story, investors are watching whether these insurance structures reduce friction for regulators and mobility partners and make it easier to run a dense network of robotaxis and robobuses. Execution around pricing, loss experience and claims handling will matter because high insurance costs or coverage gaps could offset the benefits and keep unit economics under pressure.

The additional governance detail is that Ping An Bank said the policy implements guidance issued by China's National Financial Regulatory Administration in June. AI risks are incorporated into comprehensive risk management and classified by risk level, linking board responsibility to applications already used in control functions.

Ping An Bank's interim report recorded more than 450 large-model use cases by June and 140 operational-review agents across 55 scenarios. The applications include anti-money-laundering due diligence and account review.

For investors, the policy moves the question beyond adoption toward execution. Formal oversight may help contain data, model and accountability risks, but the policy alone does not establish a financial return from the deployments. The next test is whether Ping An converts broader AI use into measurable efficiency while preserving control quality.

sum: Asian equities had a strong day on the hope that Middle East tensions are simmering down.

Let’s not bury the lead: Mainland media source, the Economic Daily, which describes itself as the “official outlet for the government to publicize its economic policies,” published an article titled “The Takeout War is Over.” This article outlines the toll that the restaurant delivery war has taken on drivers, merchants, and the balance sheets and market capitalizations of Meituan, JD.com, and Alibaba. Yesterday, we noted that the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation met with 12 internet companies, including Alibaba’s Taobao, Trip.com, Meituan, JD.com, ByteDance’s Douyin, and Kuaishou, regarding the ongoing delivery price wars. This declaration appears to be the direct result of those meetings.

Additionally, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) held a symposium yesterday on “price supervision and anti-unfair competition.” In a press release, SAMR stated “Price supervision and competition work should focus on building a strong domestic market,” and efforts should be made to “thoroughly rectify involutionary competition." Instant commerce subsidies have weighed significantly on companies' bottom lines, as adjusted net income and adjusted EPS have both cratered.

Equity strategists are stuck focusing on the MSCI China Index and earnings per share (EPS). The overall EPS level for the members of the MSCI China Consumer Discretionary Index has been decimated by Alibaba’s 39% weight and its EPS decline in 2025, as well as Meituan, which is 8% of the index, and JD.com, which is 4.7% of the index. One caveat is that Alibaba’s artificial intelligence (AI) capex has also been a factor in the steep fall in EPS. Ultimately, the restaurant delivery and instant commerce price war has affected investors’ perception of China investing, both explicitly through the individual companies' EPS declines and implicitly through the knock-on effect of strategists who focus on MSCI China EPS.

Meituan gained +13.92% on volume that increased +466% from yesterday, which is 5X the 1-year average. Alibaba gained +4.63% on volume up +70% from yesterday, though its Hong Kong stock had several big put trades, and JD.com gained +4.85% on volume up +124% from yesterday.

sum: CiDi, a major supplier of autonomous driving technology to China’s mining industry, has made an initial public offering on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to raise over US$180 million with the sale of up to 5.4 million shares. This is its second IPO attempt after a previous application in 2024 lapsed. This time it does have more heavyweights behind it including sponsors CICC, China Securities International and Ping An Securities; and five cornerstone investors, including Xiangjiang Zhicheng, Zhijia No 1 and ICBCUBS who have committed to almost 40% of the total.

CiDi plans to use the funds raised from its IPO for research and development over the next five years; and to enhance its commercialisation capabilities both domestically and internationally and to further strengthen the company’s cooperation with domestic and global clients.

In the IPO, CiDi describes itself as third in China’s autonomous mining truck market. It does not name competitors but the top company in terms of 2024 revenue from autonomous mining truck solutions, cited as ‘Company A’ is listed as having a 51.6% market share. This is EACON, which has over 2,000 autonomous mining trucks running. CiDi gives the second position with a 15.5% market share to ‘Company D’ which IM understands to be TAGE Idriver – one of the earliest entrants into the mining AHS market in China traditionally with a strong position on rigid trucks, unlike most of the others who are mainly focused on wide body trucks – though TAGE is now also focusing on that market. CiDi is in third with 12.9%.

One of CiDi’s claims to fame is that it delivered 56 autonomous mining trucks for a mining site in China in mixed traffic with~500 manned trucks, which it says is the world’s largest mixed-operation mining fleet. CiDi’s autonomous mining truck solution is called METAMINE, which it says automates labour-intensive mining operations by integrating its proprietary algorithms with widely-used intelligent driving hardware for commercial vehicles, enabling autonomous operation and remote monitoring of driverless mining trucks.

sum: Daming Electronics Co., Ltd. engages in the design, development, production, and sale of automotive body electronic and electrical control systems. It provides comprehensive solutions for automotive body electronic and electrical control systems. The company's products include driver assistance systems, cockpit central control systems, intelligent photoelectric systems, door & window control systems, and seat adjustment systems. Daming Electronics was founded by Ming Ming Zhou, Qing Sheng Ye, Ri Hui Zhou, Mei Feng Wu and Qing Xu Zhou on January 13, 1989 and is headquartered in Yueqing, China.

items.t: Car Insurance Market Size & Share - Growth Analysis 2035
sum: Car Insurance Market size was valued at USD 949.2 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 3.51 billion by the end of 2035, rising at a CAGR of 14% during the forecast period, i.e., 2026-2035. In 2026, the industry size of car insurance is estimated at USD 1.08 billion.

The car insurance market is experiencing significant growth with rising road accidents, EV adoption, and increasing consumer awareness. According to the Insurance Information Institute data in February 2025, the annual expenditure on auto insurance was USD 1,127 per policyholder in 2022, with a rise of 6.1% from 2021. The rise is mainly propelled by the increasing claim costs and increasing vehicle repair costs. Further, the inflation and higher car prices, which include the electronic components and repair costs, have contributed to a 17.8% rise in motor vehicle insurance costs in 2024. The industry is further experiencing a technology shift with the adoption of AI and data analytics for the underwriting and rate-setting process.

Further, the key trends are redefining the core operation and product structures. The advanced driver assistance systems and electric vehicles are transforming the claim landscape. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety has highlighted the effectiveness of various car crash avoidance features, with the high cost of regulating these systems post-repair presents a new cost pressure. Moreover, the regulatory priorities, such as the increased examination of pricing algorithms and claims settlement practices, require continuous compliance investment. On the other hand, these factors together drive the focus on digital transformation to enhance risk selection accuracy, claims handling, and manage combined ratios in the competitive ecosystem.

- North America in the car insurance market is expected to secure a 32.8% share by 2035, attributed to elevated vehicle ownership levels, stringent minimum coverage mandates, and rising repair costs that encourage rapid adoption of data-driven insurance models.

- Asia Pacific is projected to expand at a 6.9% CAGR through 2035, propelled by accelerating digitalization, increasing insurance awareness, and the surge of EV adoption alongside usage-based and pay-per-kilometer offerings.
